exec_narrative: Community Bank of Santa Maria is compared with 60 banks of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in California have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 8 rankable lines, five sit inside the middle half of the market, two above it (deposited-item return fee and cashier's check fee), and one below it (outgoing international wire fee). We would suggest two steps, in order of value: (1) review the deposited-item return fee, which sits well above the market range; the peer median of $5 is the reference point; (2) check that the overdraft fee is published where customers can find it.

callouts.title: Deposited-item return fee — $18
callouts.stat: Peer median $5 · middle half $5–$10 · range $3–$12 · 100th percentile · n=15
callouts.body: Published as “Returned deposited item.” At $18 it is 3.6× the $5 peer median. This fee falls on the depositor for a check someone else wrote, which makes it a frequent example in fee-fairness criticism. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $5 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Cashier's check fee — $8
callouts.stat: Peer median $5 · middle half $5–$7 · range $3–$20 · 82nd percentile · n=11
callouts.body: Published as “Cashier's Checks (Customers).” At $8 it is $3 above the $5 peer median. It is infrequent and mostly a perception item. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $5 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Outgoing international wire fee — $40
callouts.stat: Peer median $50 · middle half $46.25–$61.25 · 25th percentile · n=8
callouts.body: Published as “Wire Transfer - International Outgoing.” A customer-favorable price on a low-volume line. No action is indicated unless it is an old price that was never revisited, in which case the peer median of $50 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Fees we could not find in your published schedule
callouts.body: Absence here means the line was not in the documents listed in § 06, not that you do not charge it. Regulators and comparison sites increasingly expect the full consumer fee schedule to be posted in one place.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Community Bank of Santa Maria with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
